title: The Koide balance r=1/2: count the paired mode once or twice
plain: The three lepton masses obey Koide's rule only if one paired part of the mass matrix is counted once. Counted twice the rule becomes Q=1, which makes two of the three leptons massless. The lattice gives both readings equal standing and every natural mechanism tried lands on 'twice' or is blind. Nothing derived picks 'once'; what is left is an extra premise.
same_as: gravity-source / statistical-bridge lane (reflection pairing, formation weight)

title: The Brannen phase delta=2/9: from an exact fraction to an angle in radians
plain: The phase that splits the electron from the muon comes out of the lattice as the exact fraction 2/9, a counting density at a cube corner. The measured value is 0.2222 in radians, within 1 sigma of 2/9. No result shows that this fraction is the angle in radians rather than a fraction of a turn or half-turn. Every angle the lattice gives natively is a rational multiple of pi, never a bare 2/9.

title: Carrier and species bridge: the mass matrix, the square-root rule and the labels are supplied
plain: The masses come from a 3x3 matrix on the three cube-corner states. That matrix is supplied, not derived: the free lattice has no mixing between corners, the lattice cannot say which corner or mixture is the electron, muon or tau, and nothing derives why a mass is the square of a matrix eigenvalue. So 'this matrix describes the charged leptons' is an identification made by hand.

title: The absolute lepton scale (a^2, equivalently y_tau) is a free number with two unexplained numerical matches
plain: Even with the right shape, the overall size of the lepton masses is a free number. Two coincidences exist: one ties it to the W mass divided by 256 to 0.03%; the other gives the tau mass from the electroweak scale and couplings to 0.02%. Neither is derived. The exponent 4 in 256 is unexplained, and the Ward-identity route that worked for the top quark is closed for leptons.
same_as: top-Yukawa lane (contrast: Ward boundary works there)
electroweak hierarchy lane (supplies v and alpha_LM)

title: Symmetry breaking S3 to C3 and the handedness choice
plain: If the lattice's full axis-permutation symmetry were exact, the three leptons could have only two different masses. Three distinct masses need that symmetry cut down to cyclic rotations, and the cut has been traced to one yes/no handedness choice. The same choice fixes which sign of the phase is physical. No derivation forces that handedness; the owner has parked the question.
same_as: gravity-sign orientation datum (reading, branch titles only)

title: Why the leptons sit at r=1/2 and the quarks do not (sector spread)
plain: The balance number is 1/2 for charged leptons but about 0.62 for down-type and 0.83 for up-type quarks (at a common scale). Any single rule that gives leptons 1/2 gives quarks 1/2 too unless something distinguishes the sectors. The tested candidates (colour, gauge holonomy, entropy, running, a fixed point) either cannot separate the sectors or put them in the wrong order. The value per sector is a free input.

title: Which mass scheme and scale the Koide relation is claimed at (latent)
plain: The measured masses fit Koide to 6 parts in a million only as pole (physical) masses. Converting the same masses to a running scheme at high scale moves Q by about 1.2 parts in a thousand, 200 times bigger. The repository never says at which scale or in which scheme its derived r=1/2 would hold. It is a bookkeeping gap that becomes a test failure the moment r is derived.

title: Cross-sector link: is the charged-lepton counting channel the one that fixes the quark determinant phase?
plain: Strong-CP (why the neutron has no electric dipole moment) is supposed to follow from the quark mass phase being zero. The lane's registered claim is that the same counting channel that fixes the lepton value also fixes that quark phase. That link is not derived, so closing the lepton counting bit would not by itself settle strong-CP.
